related_questions.question: How to price donations for tax purposes?

text_blocks.snippet: To accurately price donated items for tax purposes, you'll generally need to determine their fair market value (FMV), which is the price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller. For items like clothing and household goods, you can often find value guides from organizations like Goodwill or Salvation Army. For more valuable items or if you're unsure, consider getting a professional appraisal. Remember to keep detailed records of your donations, including receipts and a list of items with their estimated FMV.

list.title: 1. Understand Fair Market Value (FMV):
list.snippet: FMV is the price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller when neither is under pressure to buy or sell, and both have reasonable knowledge of the relevant facts.

list.title: 2. Use Donation Value Guides:
list.snippet: Organizations like Goodwill and Salvation Army offer guides that provide estimated values for common donated items like clothing, household goods, and furniture.

list.title: 3. Consider Item Condition:
list.snippet: The condition of your donated items significantly impacts their value. Gently used items will be worth less than new or like-new items.

list.title: 4. Check Online Marketplaces:
list.snippet: For items not listed in donation guides, you can research similar items for sale on online marketplaces like eBay or Craigslist to get an idea of their FMV.

list.title: 5. Consult Professional Appraisals:
list.snippet: For valuable items, artwork, antiques, or when you're unsure about the value, consider getting a professional appraisal from a qualified appraiser.

list.title: 6. Keep Detailed Records:
list.snippet: Maintain a list of all donated items, their estimated FMV, and the date of donation. Also, keep the receipts from the charitable organization.

list.title: 7. IRS Form 8283:
list.snippet: If your noncash donation exceeds $500, you must file IRS Form 8283 "Noncash Charitable Contributions," according to the IRS.

list.title: 8. Donations Over $5,000:
list.snippet: If your noncash donation (excluding publicly traded securities) exceeds $5,000, the charitable organization may also need to acknowledge the contribution on Form 8283.

list.title: 9. Tax Software:
list.snippet: Some tax software, like TurboTax, can help you determine the value of your donated items and even import the information into your tax return.

list.title: 10. Consult a Tax Professional:
list.snippet: For complex situations or if you have questions, it's always best to consult with a tax professional or certified public accountant (CPA) for personalized advice.
